title: A COVENANT AS SURE AS SALT

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But you must not redeem the firstborn of a cow, a sheep or a goat; they are holy. Splash their blood against the altar and burn their fat as a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the Lord. Their meat is to be yours, just as the breast of the wave offering and the right thigh are yours. Whatever is set aside from the holy offerings the Israelites present to the Lord I give to you and your sons and daughters as your perpetual share. It is an everlasting covenant of salt before the Lord for both you and your offspring." — Num 18:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God calls His provision for the priests "an everlasting covenant of salt." What a striking phrase. Salt preserves; it does not spoil or fade. To call something a covenant of salt was to declare it lasting, permanent, unbreakable. God was binding Himself by a promise that would not decay with time.

This tells us something wonderful about God's character. When He makes a commitment, He keeps it. His promises are not like ours, so often broken or forgotten. They are like salt — enduring, dependable, preserved through every generation. The priests could count on God's provision not just for a season but perpetually, because God had bound Himself to it.

How steadying it is to serve a God whose promises are sure. We live in a world of shifting commitments, where people change their minds and pledges dissolve. But God's covenants stand firm. What He has promised, He will do, and time only proves His faithfulness rather than eroding it.

Every covenant God made pointed toward the greatest covenant of all, sealed in the blood of Jesus. At the Last Supper He spoke of "the new covenant in my blood" — an everlasting covenant that can never be broken, guaranteeing our forgiveness and our place with God forever. If a covenant of salt secured the priests' provision, how much more securely does the blood of Christ secure our salvation. His promises to you are as sure as salt, and surer still. Rest in the unbreakable faithfulness of God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does it steady you to know God's promises never fade?
2. Where do you need to trust God's faithfulness rather than shifting circumstances?
3. What comfort do you find in the everlasting new covenant sealed in Christ's blood?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that Your promises are as enduring as salt, unbreakable and sure. In a world of shifting commitments, help me rest in Your faithfulness. Thank You for the everlasting new covenant sealed in the blood of Christ. Amen.
